design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 of seller_payouts_reserves_chargebacks (category payout), scenario env_0054_ecommerce_marketplace_operator.

[Step 0 — draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]}. Root payout_ext_negative_balance_settlement takes 6 factors, prerequisite payout_ext_won_chargeback_fee_return takes 4. Occupied by task 0: payout_ext_scheduled_payout_limit, payout_ext_won_chargeback_debit_return, payout_ext_instant_fee_posting, payout_ext_on_demand_payout and their four tools. Claimed here (disjoint): the seller-authorised card settlement of a negative balance (payout_negative_balance_charge, user tool pay_negative_balance_by_card_47b519ae) and the fee component of a won chargeback reversal (payout_chargeback_reversal fee_returned, agent tool return_won_chargeback_fee_5c062853). With these two the difficulty's six extended policies are all claimed; no idle policy or tool remains.

[Why this is a good test] The seller asks to pay off a negative balance with her card. The figure she saw (-869.00) is not what settles it under the published rule: the settlement rule says a card settlement is not charged until every won chargeback case with a fee return due carries that entry. Case CB-20260814-0391 was won on signature_confirmation evidence and its debit was returned on 2026-09-22, but its 20.00 fee was never returned; the agent must read the fee-return rule (which returns part of the fee on plans that do not normally return it), compute 7.50 over evidence, standing, chargeback history and account age, book it, and only then compute the settlement on the reduced deficit with six further factors.

[Problem tree] root payout_ext_negative_balance_settlement (user). One edge, value_input, gate deficit, form state. Sentence (negated direction, as a collections desk states a charge waiting on a correction): "A card settlement of a negative balance is not charged until every won chargeback case with a fee return due carries that fee-return entry on the payments ledger." Condition: every won case with a positive fee return has a fee_returned reversal entry. Opening evidence: dispute on CB-20260814-0391 won (signature_confirmation), fee 20.00 charged 2026-08-14, debit_returned entry 640.00 on 2026-09-22, no fee_returned entry. Only write that books a fee_returned reversal: return_won_chargeback_fee_5c062853 (the debit-return tool of task 0 books debit_returned). Four-point test: connective "not ... until"; record-visible state named in ledger words; no tool/id/code token; scope "every won case with a fee return due". Skip-run: settlement 1,221.75 instead of 1,212.75. Order: fee return, then settlement. User write: paying one's own debt with one's own card is the seller disposing of her own affairs.

[Factor card — fee return, 4 factors; baseline: fee returned only when the plan returns it on a win — Payments Starter does not -> 0.00]
 evidence_fee_share_rule (parameter): Starter does not return the fee on a win and the evidence is signature_confirmation -> 1.0 (baseline plan rule 0 -> 0.00). standing_history_scale (parameter, cross standing): Developing Seller Level -> 0.5 (baseline -> 15.00). chargeback_history_scale (parameter): 2 chargebacks in twelve months -> 0.75 (baseline -> 10.00). history_combination (method): account 248 days -> multiplied (0.375) (baseline smaller -> 10.00). Result 20.00 x 1.0 x 0.375 = 7.50. Near-miss: the 2026-10-06 chargeback on CB-20261006-0618 has no dispute and earns nothing.
[Factor card — card settlement, 6 factors; baseline: the deficit 861.50]
 refund_window (method): account 248 days (under 365) -> the one-month window (500.00 vs 2,930.00, 17.1 percent) and the two-month window (760.00 vs 10,100.00, 7.5 percent) are compared and the smaller share, two months, is used (baseline last month -> 1,261.75). risk_top_up (parameter, multi-source: level AND unreturned chargeback count, cross standing): Developing with count 1 (2 debited in six months less 1 returned-debit entry) -> 0.20 (-> 1,040.45). Near-miss: two chargebacks were debited in six months but one returned-debit entry stands in those months, so the count is 1, not 2. negative_history (parameter): the automatic card charge of 2026-05-19 succeeded, none declined -> 25.00 (-> 1,187.75). refund_cover_rule (parameter): 7.5 percent -> 0.10 x 760.00 = 76.00 (-> 1,136.75). account_age_cushion (parameter): under 365 days -> 50.00 (-> 1,162.75). upcoming_store_fee_rule (parameter, cross selling): Basic Store monthly, next billing 2026-10-20 within 7 days -> 27.95 (-> 1,184.80). Result 861.50 x 1.20 + 25.00 + 76.00 + 50.00 + 27.95 = 1,212.75; all-baseline 861.50.
 Cross-difficulty evidence seeded and read: standing_records (Developing Seller Level, good_standing), selling_plans (Basic Store, monthly, next billing 2026-10-20).

[Base-invariant card] payout_chargeback_reversal: payout_chargebacks.dispute_won — dispute_status won on CB-20260814-0391 -> true. payout_negative_balance_charge: payout_negative_balance has no gate; its automatic charge applies after more than 14 days negative (Payments Starter); the balance has been negative since 2026-10-06 (10 days), so no automatic charge is owed and, because 10 days is within the 14 card charge days, the seller-authorised settlement applies. Selling plan restriction after 30 days negative is not reached.
[Business-object card] Fee return: case CB-20260814-0391, correlation chargeback_case_id; its fee 20.00; excluded: case CB-20261006-0618 (no dispute). Settlement: the account's deficit after the fee return; refund debits of the window (2026-09-02 260.00, 2026-09-24 180.00, 2026-10-08 320.00); the May refunds lie outside the window.

[World] 140 ledger rows from 2026-02-10 simulated under Payments Starter rules: 24 orders with sale credit, delivery reserve (21 days after delivery, +7 at 1,000.00 or more) and a 10 percent rolling reserve released after 90 days; Wednesday payouts of the payable amount when at least 25.00; Basic Store fees on the 20th; refunds of 4,900.00 and 1,120.00 on 2026-05-04 took the balance to -1,589.00, which stayed negative more than 14 days and was charged automatically for 899.00 on 2026-05-19; chargeback CB-20260814-0391 (640.00 + 20.00 fee, dispute 2026-08-16 won, debit returned 2026-09-22 under the debit-return rule with no response fee because it was the only dispute in twelve months); chargeback CB-20261006-0618 (5,400.00 + 20.00) took the balance negative on 2026-10-06; balance -869.00, reserved 4,194.00.

[Persona] Ingrid, friendly and a little anxious; volunteers only her goal and the dashboard impression of about minus eight hundred seventy (true). Verification by phone 5125550467 and tax ID 6915 (ZIP 78745 in reserve). Passive: accepts the amount, asks once why it is more than she saw, pays herself when handed over, reads back the result, ends. Her only line about prior steps is reactive (only if the agent says something must be booked first). No prerequisite named or hinted (the word chargeback does not occur in the persona).

[Standard solution / verification] Reads: find_customers(name) -> verify_customer_identity(phone, tax_id_last4) -> find_payments_accounts -> find_payments_ledger -> find_chargeback_disputes -> find_orders(seller) -> find_seller_standing -> find_selling_plans. Writes: return_won_chargeback_fee (CB-20260814-0391, 7.50); the seller's pay_negative_balance_by_card (1,212.75). The generator replays the gold with the real tools and evaluates each compute through check_compute's evaluator on the handling-time world: 7.5 and 1212.75, factor sensitivities as above, baseline results 0.0 and 861.5.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the published rules: the settlement waits on fee returns of won cases -> disputes lookup shows one won case -> ledger shows no fee return on it -> fee-return rule gives 7.50 -> deficit 861.50 -> settlement rule gives 1,212.75. One reading only.

[Round 2 — responses by audit item]
 T1-1 / F-1 (window-only method factor): refund_window now compares, for accounts under 365 days, the one-month and two-month windows and uses the one whose refund debits are the smaller share of its sale credits (a selection between candidates, not a window length). This account sits on that tier: 17.1 percent vs 7.5 percent -> two months; refund cover 76.00 and the settlement 1,212.75 are unchanged; baseline (one month) still 1,261.75.
 F-3: the fee-return evidence tiers now apply only on plans that do not return the fee on a win (Payments Starter here), so on Payments Enterprise every case sits on the plan-rule fall-through and no tier collapses; this case still takes 1.0 -> 7.50.
 O-5: the settlement rule now defines the unreturned chargeback count exactly as computed (chargebacks debited in six months less returned-debit entries booked in those six months); here 2 - 1 = 1, the same as the per-case reading.
 O-9: the upcoming store fee now requires the next billing date to be the settlement date or up to 7 days after it (here 2026-10-20, 4 days after).
 O-10 / O-T1-a: the settlement rule now applies only while the balance has been below zero for no more than the plan's card charge days, after which only the automatic charge of the full deficit applies, so the two never compete; here 10 of 14 days. The amount above the deficit is the policy's stated working-balance top-up (it stays in the balance, and with 4,194.00 still reserved the 351.25 left after the settlement is not payable until reserves release); the base event wording 'charged to bring a negative balance back to zero' describes the purpose of the charge and is met (the balance does return to zero or more). No value change.
 O-T1-b (persona disposition line): replaced by a purely reactive line.
 World: unchanged and already producible under the charter (the auditor recomputed it); under the round-2 debit-return rule the 2026-09-22 return is still 640.00 (signature evidence -> full debit; the only dispute of twelve months -> no response fee). The fee return owed since the win was never booked; booking it is this task's prerequisite.
user_scenario:
You are Ingrid Oyelaran-Pike, owner of Pike & Fern Candle Works LLC, a small candle workshop that sells hand-poured candles to boutiques through Northloop Marketplace. You are calling the seller support desk on Friday afternoon between batches; you are friendly, a little anxious about money, and you tend to explain yourself in full sentences.

Why you are calling: your Northloop Payments balance has gone negative this month. When you looked this morning it showed roughly minus eight hundred and seventy dollars. You do not want it hanging over the account, so you want to pay it off today with the card you have on file with Northloop, rather than waiting for Northloop to charge the card later.

You know the payment has to be authorised by you, so when the agent tells you the amount and hands the card payment over to you, you make the payment yourself with the payments account reference and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back what you see afterwards. Only if the agent says something has to be booked or corrected on the account first do you react to it: you then tell them that is fine and to go ahead, and you do not ask for the details.

To identify yourself: your name is Ingrid Oyelaran-Pike and the business is Pike & Fern Candle Works LLC. When the agent asks for verification details, you give your mobile number 5125550467 and the last four digits of your business tax ID, 6915. If they need one more detail you can also give your billing ZIP code, 78745. You do not know internal reference numbers.

Only if the agent asks which card to use, you say the card on file ending 7782. If the agent asks whether you want to pay a different amount, you say you want to pay whatever the desk says settles it today.

When the agent tells you the amount, you accept it. If it is more than the roughly eight hundred and seventy dollars you saw, you ask once, politely, why it is more than that, listen, and accept the explanation without bargaining. You never propose any figure, rule or step yourself.

Once you have made the payment and read back the result, you thank the agent warmly and end the call; you have nothing else to raise.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 7.50 — chargeback fee charged on the case 20.00 x evidence fee-return share 1.0 (Payments Starter does not return the fee on a win and the dispute was won on signature_confirmation evidence) x combined history multiplier 0.375. The standing history multiplier is 0.5 (Developing Seller Level); the chargeback history multiplier is 0.75 (exactly 2 chargebacks debited in twelve months: 2026-08-14 and 2026-10-06); the payments account was opened 2026-02-10, 248 days before, so the two are multiplied together (0.5 x 0.75 = 0.375). 20.00 x 1.0 x 0.375 = 7.50.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 1212.75 — deficit 861.50 (balance -869.00 + fee return 7.50 = -861.50); the balance has been below zero since 2026-10-06, 10 days, within the 14 card charge days of Payments Starter, so a seller-authorised settlement applies. Risk top-up share 0.20: Developing Seller Level and unreturned chargeback count 1 (2 chargebacks debited in six months, 1 returned-debit entry in those months). Negative-history cushion 25.00: one card charge for a negative balance in twelve months (2026-05-19, succeeded), none declined. Refund cover 76.00: the account is 248 days old, so the one-month window (500.00 against 2,930.00, 17.1 percent) and the two-month window (760.00 against 10,100.00, 7.5 percent) are compared and the smaller share, two months, is used -> 0.10 x 760.00. New-account cushion 50.00 (account under 365 days). Upcoming store fee 27.95: Basic Store billed monthly, next billing 2026-10-20, 4 days after. 861.50 x 1.20 + 25.00 + 76.00 + 50.00 + 27.95 = 1,212.75.

edges.condition: Every chargeback case whose dispute status is won and on which the fee-return rule gives a fee above zero has a chargeback reversal entry of the fee_returned movement on the payments ledger.
edges.policy_source: A card settlement of a negative balance is not charged until every won chargeback case with a fee return due carries that fee-return entry on the payments ledger.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: Case CB-20260814-0391 has a won dispute on signature_confirmation evidence, so the fee-return rule gives a positive fee return (7.50), and the ledger carries its 20.00 fee and its returned debit but no reversal entry of the fee_returned movement.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The fee-return write books a payout_chargeback_reversal entry (fee_returned, 7.50) on case CB-20260814-0391; the balance rises from -869.00 to -861.50 and the deficit to 861.50.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite: the fee return must precede the settlement (the settlement sentence waits on it) and there is no parallel prerequisite to order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the fee return leaves the deficit at 869.00; the settlement becomes 1,221.75 instead of 1,212.75 (869.00 x 1.20 + 178.95), and the terminal ledger lacks the 7.50 fee-return entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only to pay off the negative balance with the card on file. It does not mention any chargeback, dispute, fee or correction and does not ask whether something must be settled first; its only line about prior steps is purely reactive: only if the agent says something must be booked or corrected first does she say that is fine.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: pay_negative_balance_by_card_47b519ae books the card charge and moves the balance for whatever amount it is given; it reads the account only to copy the customer and the balance, never checks fee returns, chargebacks or dates, and returns no error or hint. return_won_chargeback_fee_5c062853 books its single entry likewise.
